# ethereum-optimism/optimism Weekly Report (Apr 12 - 18, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, development focused heavily on advancing the **Layer 2 Chain Management (L2CM)** system and the **Osaka/Jovian** hardfork specifications. Significant progress was made in refining the `op-node` and `kona` stacks, particularly regarding EL-sync reliability and audit-driven security fixes for interop contracts. The introduction of Sequencer Defined Metering (SDM) metadata and the migration of critical fault proof tests to the `op-acceptance-tests` suite signal a continued push toward protocol maturity and Superchain scalability.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Core Protocol & Hardfork Readiness
The team implemented several foundational changes to support upcoming Ethereum and Optimism-specific upgrades.
*   **Osaka & Jovian Support:** New PRs introduced support for EIPs including EIP-7951 (P256VERIFY precompile), EIP-7939 (CLZ opcode), and gas limit caps ([#20071](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20071), [#20073](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20073), [#20070](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20070)).
*   **Sequencer Defined Metering (SDM):** Introduced a new post-execution transaction type to carry SDM metadata across `alloy-op-evm` and `op-reth`, essential for future metering mechanisms ([#19954](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19954)).
*   **Holocene Compatibility:** Enforced strict frame ordering in the `ChannelAssembler` to align with post-Holocene behavior ([#20011](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20011)).

### Node Infrastructure & Sync Improvements
Enhancements to `op-node` and `op-supernode` focused on synchronization correctness and configuration flexibility.
*   **EL-Sync Retraction:** The `op-node` now supports offsetting derived safe/finalized states during EL-sync, resolving long-standing UX issues regarding ancestor-based safety ([#19972](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19972)).
*   **Interop Activation:** Updated `op-supernode` to derive interop activation timestamps directly from rollup configurations by default ([#19938](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19938)).
*   **Dependency Management:** Resolved a cyclic dependency in `op-deployer` by introducing a new `devfeatures` package in `op-core` ([#19970](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19970)).

### Kona & Fault Proofs
The `kona` stack received critical updates following audit findings and testing requirements.
*   **Consensus Fixes:** Addressed issues in `kona` regarding Brotli activation checks and precompile versions for Jovian specs to prevent consensus deviations ([#20004](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20004), [#20003](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20003)).
*   **Testing Migration:** Successfully migrated `TestInteropFaultProofs` and deposit message execution tests to the `op-acceptance-tests` suite using the devstack DSL ([#20047](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20047), [#20046](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20046)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **L2CM & NUT Consolidation:** Multiple issues regarding the Network Upgrade Transaction (NUT) bundle system were closed as work was consolidated into a primary tracking issue for `kona-node` ([#18831](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18831), [#18835](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18835)).
*   **Cleanup:** Successfully removed dead Solidity code in `contracts-bedrock` and resolved the `devfeatures` cyclic dependency ([#20040](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20040), [#19151](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19151)).
*   **Interop Portal:** Progress on OPCM v2 was marked by closing issues related to `DelayedWETH` allowances and snapshot removals ([#18381](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18381)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **L2CM Audit Follow-ups:** A surge of new issues tracks audit findings, including gas overstatements in `ExecuteNUTBundle` ([#20076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20076)) and missing access control guards on the `OptimismMintableERC20Factory` ([#20080](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20080)).
*   **Codebase Hygiene:** A large-scale effort is underway to remove orphaned CLI tools, deprecated Go flags, and unreferenced Docker artifacts ([#20042](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20042), [#20036](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20036)).
*   **Flaky Tests:** `TestInvalidPayloadThroughCLP2P` remains an active blocker, with investigations focusing on failed assertions during fault injection ([#19968](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19968)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week was characterized by high-intensity review cycles surrounding **L2 Interop Contracts**. Discussions moved from GitHub to Slack to finalize the operational logic of the `CrossL2Inbox` ([#20008](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20008)). There is also a clear trend toward standardizing the Rust development environment, evidenced by the automation of toolchains via `mise` and the refactoring of shared binary tooling for `kona-host`, which facilitates easier contributions across the Rust-based components of the stack.
